proposals.expected_failure_mode: May under-represent systematic admission lag; can show slight phase error around rapid rise/peak if hospitalizations consistently trail infections.
proposals.rationale: Anchor baseline per constraints: parsimonious SEIRS with contemporaneous I observation as a stable proxy for weekly hospitalization-rate dynamics when explicit admission lag is uncertain and longer delays were unstable.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true lag is near-zero or variable over the season, a fixed 1-week delay can misalign peak timing and degrade fit/forecast stability.
proposals.rationale: Adds minimal timing flexibility (1-week lag) consistent with surveillance note while respecting robustness constraint against longer delays; keeps dynamics non-fractional to reduce rolling-split instability.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Greater parameter sensitivity/identifiability issues can increase rolling variability; may overfit transient fluctuations and yield less robust forecasts than the non-fractional counterparts.
proposals.rationale: Single constrained fractional candidate for direct comparison against the non-fractional delayed baseline; may better capture moderate peakiness and high rate scale via heavier-tailed/long-memory-like dynamics without adding compartments.
